chunks: Allah (swt) narrated to me Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abdillah ibn al-Mughira, from al-Abbas ibn 'Amir, from Jabr al-Makfuuf, from Abu al-Samit, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) say: Whoever visits al-Husayn (peace be upon him) walking, Allah writes for him for every step a thousand good deeds, erases from him a thousand bad deeds, and raises him a thousand degrees.
So when you reach the Euphrates, perform ghusl, hang your sandals, and walk barefoot, and walk with the walk of a humble servant.
So when you reach the gate of al-Ha'ir, say 'Allahu Akbar' four times, offer prayer there, and ask Allah for your needs.

key_terms.الْحَائِرِ: The area surrounding the shrine of Imam al-Husayn in Karbala
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ (ع): Imam al-Husayn, grandson of the Prophet Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What are the rewards and ritual steps for visiting Imam Husayn's shrine according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records this foundational hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) that establishes the theological framework for Ziyarat al-Jaish, linking physical pilgrimage to spiritual purification. The specific instruction to perform ghusl at the Euphrates (Al-Furat) and walk barefoot reflects the historical context of Karbala’s geography and the concept of 'khushu’' (humility) before the Imam, transforming the journey into a reenactment of devotion. This practice underscores the Shia belief that the physical act of visiting the shrine serves as a means of drawing near to God, with each step serving as a tangible record of merit.
